items.title: An oxidized ribonucleotide 8-oxoGTP drives neuroinflammation and accelerates cognitive decline.
items.authors: Jin Li; Zhen-He Wang; Jia-Xin Pan; Zhe-Li Jiang; Rui Li; Xu-Fan Gao; Gang Sheng; Zi-Hui Wang
items.abstract: Oxidative stress is a hallmark of aging and a key driver of neurodegenerative diseases. While much attention has been given to oxidative damage of macromolecules, the functional consequences of oxidizing the abundant nucleotide triphosphate (NTP) pool remain largely unknown. Here, we identify oxidized GTP (8-oxoGTP)-a major product of NTP oxidation-not as a mere marker of damage, but as an endogenous signaling molecule that drives microglial activation and neuroinflammation. 8-oxoGTP accumulated in the aging mouse brain, and its elevation was sufficient to induce synaptic dysfunction, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline. Mechanistically, 8-oxoGTP functioned as a potent activator of heterotrimeric G proteins, binding more strongly to Gα subunits than GTP itself, triggering Src kinase/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB signaling in microglia, leading to pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reactive oxygen species generation, and neurotoxicity. Pharmacological inhibition of Src family kinases rescued the neuroinflammatory and cognitive phenotypes induced by 8-oxoGTP. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking nucleotide oxidation to age-associated neurodegenerative processes.

items.abstract_cn: 氧化应激是衰老的标志，也是神经退行性疾病的关键驱动因素。尽管人们对大分子的氧化损伤给予了很多关注，但氧化丰富的三磷酸核苷酸（NTP）池的功能后果仍然很大程度上未知。在这里，我们确定了氧化 GTP (8-oxoGTP)——NTP 氧化的主要产物——不仅仅是损伤标记，而是驱动小胶质细胞激活和神经炎症的内源信号分子。 8-oxoGTP 在衰老小鼠大脑中积累，其升高足以诱发突触功能障碍、tau 蛋白过度磷酸化、神经元损失和认知能力下降。从机制上讲，8-oxoGTP 作为异三聚体 G 蛋白的有效激活剂，与 Gα 亚基的结合比 GTP 本身更强，触发小胶质细胞中的 Src 激酶/MAPK/Akt/NF-κB 信号传导，导致促炎细胞因子的产生、活性氧的产生和神经毒性。 Src 家族激酶的药理学抑制可挽救 8-oxoGTP 诱导的神经炎症和认知表型。我们的研究结果揭示了一种以前未被认识的机制，将核苷酸氧化与年龄相关的神经退行性过程联系起来。

items.title: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound activates Piezo1 to restore brain lymphatic drainage and improve outcomes in traumatic brain injury mice.
items.authors: Shuo Wang; Bo Wang; Yuchang Wang; Meng Nie; Jiangyuan Yuan; Chenrui Wu; Liang Mi; Bo Chen
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Meningeal lymphatic vessels (mLVs) are specialized lymphatic structures that drain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and facilitate immune surveillance of the central nervous system. This drainage system is impaired after traumatic brain injury (TBI); mLVs undergo structural regression, and CSF outflow to peripheral lymphoid tissues is markedly slowed. The resulting accumulation of hyperphosphorylated tau, amyloid-β, and inflammatory mediators drives sustained neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. The neuroprotective effect of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) in TBI mice has been previously demonstrated, however, its impact on brain lymphatic drainage is unclear. METHODS: Here, we employed a controlled cortical impact (CCI) mouse model of TBI combined with serial LIPUS stimulation to investigate its therapeutic potential for mLV function. RESULTS: LIPUS restored neurological function in TBI mice, improving motor coordination and spatial/recognition memory while attenuating tau pathology, Aβ burden, and astrocyte reactivity. Mechanistically, LIPUS activated Piezo1 on meningeal lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs), triggering a downstream signaling cascade that promoted LEC proliferation and migration in vitro and restored lymphatic coverage and drainage function in vivo. To identify the critical mediator of this process, we examined the pathway's downstream components and found that vascular endothelial growth factor C (VEGFC) served as the critical downstream effector: VEGFC overexpression rescued meningeal lymphatic restoration and CSF drainage. CONCLUSIONS: These results establish LIPUS as a non-invasive therapeutic strategy that functionally restores brain lymphatic drainage after TBI, representing a promising preclinical therapeutic strategy for proteinopathy-associated neurological diseases that warrants further optimization for clinical translation.

items.title_cn: 低强度脉冲超声激活 Piezo1 来恢复脑部淋巴引流并改善创伤性脑损伤小鼠的预后。
items.abstract_cn: 背景：脑膜淋巴管（mLV）是一种特殊的淋巴结构，可排出脑脊液（CSF）并促进中枢神经系统的免疫监视。脑外伤 (TBI) 后，该引流系统会受损； mLV 发生结构退化，脑脊液向外周淋巴组织的流出明显减慢。由此产生的过度磷酸化 tau、β 淀粉样蛋白和炎症介质的积累会导致持续的神经炎症和认知能力下降。低强度脉冲超声 (LIPUS) 对 TBI 小鼠的神经保护作用已被证实，但其对脑淋巴引流的影响尚不清楚。方法：在这里，我们采用 TBI 的受控皮质冲击 (CCI) 小鼠模型结合连续 LIPUS 刺激来研究其对 mLV 功能的治疗潜力。结果：LIPUS 恢复了 TBI 小鼠的神经功能，改善了运动协调性和空间/识别记忆，同时减轻了 tau 病理学、Aβ 负荷和星形胶质细胞反应性。从机制上讲，LIPUS 激活脑膜淋巴内皮细胞 (LEC) 上的 Piezo1，触发下游信号级联，促进 LEC 体外增殖和迁移，并恢复体内淋巴覆盖和引流功能。为了确定这一过程的关键介质，我们检查了该通路的下游成分，发现血管内皮生长因子 C (VEGFC) 是关键的下游效应器：VEGFC 过度表达可挽救脑膜淋巴恢复和脑脊液引流。结论：这些结果表明，LIPUS 是一种非侵入性治疗策略，可在功能上恢复 TBI 后的脑淋巴引流，代表了一种有前景的蛋白质病相关神经系统疾病的临床前治疗策略，值得进一步优化临床转化。

items.title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke.
items.authors: Yueman Zhang; Yonghui Chen; Yue Cheng; Ruqi Li; Weijie Chen; Yan Li; Qiuyue Fan; Yuxi Zhou
items.abstract: Brain myeloid cells, including infiltrating monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) and microglia, play critical roles in ischemic brain injury, clearing debris and shaping neuroinflammation and neurological outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, using single-cell RNA sequencing and fate mapping with an MDM-specific Ms4a3creERT2-Ai14 mouse line, we identified serotonin receptor Htr2b+ MDMs as a crucial cell population involved in resolving neuroinflammation within the ischemic penumbra. Htr2b+ MDMs significantly accumulate in the peri-infarct region and exhibit enhanced phagocytosis and inflammation-resolving gene signatures. Mechanistically, Htr2b activation promotes nuclear translocation of Tfe3, a key lysosomal regulator, enhancing lysosomal biogenesis and supporting phagocytic activity. MDM-specific Htr2b ablation impairs debris clearance, exacerbates neuroinflammation and ischemic injury, whereas pharmacological agonism or Tfe3 activation restores lysosomal biogenesis in brain MDMs and improves post-stroke outcomes. Thus we demonstrate a previously unrecognized Htr2b+ MDM subset that integrates serotonin signaling to license intrinsic phagocytic function, alleviating ischemic brain injury.

items.title_cn: 血清素信号通过 Htr2b 增强脑巨噬细胞的吞噬作用，减轻中风后的脑损伤。
items.abstract_cn: 脑髓细胞，包括浸润性单核细胞源性巨噬细胞 (MDM) 和小胶质细胞，在缺血性脑损伤、清除碎片以及塑造神经炎症和神经系统结果中发挥着关键作用。然而潜在的机制仍不清楚。在这里，我们利用单细胞 RNA 测序和 MDM 特异性 Ms4a3creERT2-Ai14 小鼠系的命运图谱，确定了血清素受体 Htr2b+ MDM 是参与解决缺血半影内神经炎症的关键细胞群。 Htr2b+ MDM 在梗死周围区域显着积累，并表现出增强的吞噬作用和炎症解决基因特征。从机制上讲，Htr2b 激活促进关键溶酶体调节因子 Tfe3 的核转位，增强溶酶体生物发生并支持吞噬细胞活性。 MDM 特异性 Htr2b 消融会损害碎片清除，加剧神经炎症和缺血性损伤，而药理学激动或 Tfe3 激活可恢复脑 MDM 中的溶酶体生物合成并改善中风后结局。因此，我们证明了一个以前未被识别的 Htr2b+ MDM 子集，它整合了血清素信号传导以许可内在的吞噬功能，从而减轻缺血性脑损伤。

items.title: The characteristics of perivascular proinflammation in 4-repeat tauopathies.
items.authors: Mu-Hui Fu; Gokhan Uruk; Rodolfo G Gatto; R Ross Reichard; Jennifer L Whitwell; Keith A Josephs
items.abstract: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD) are both neurodegenerative diseases characterized by aggregates composed of 4-repeat (4R) tau protein. They have distinct neuropathological features and classic clinical symptoms; however, the signs and symptoms overlap across the two syndromes. Accumulating evidence suggests that dysregulated immune response is a major contributing factor to neurodegeneration but its role in 4R-tauopathies remains undetermined. The aim is to explore the involvement of neuroinflammation from a vascular perspective in 4R-tauopathies. Autopsies from four controls, three PSP, and three CBD cases were assessed. Samples were obtained from the superior/middle frontal gyrus (S/M-FG) and basal ganglia (BG). Immunofluorescence staining included neuroinflammatory markers: glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 (Iba1), cluster of differentiation 68 (CD68); vascular markers: collagen type IV (ColIV), monocarboxylate transporter-1 (MCT1), and α-smooth muscle actin (αSMA). Maximally projected confocal z-stack images of vasculature were used as a mask to quantify total perivascular GFAP+/Iba1+/CD68+ labeling. GFAP immunoreactivity ratio between MCT1 and αSMA double labeled arteries and veins was quantified to further differentiate venular and arteriolar involvement into proinflammatory activation. Both PSP and CBD had widespread perivascular proinflammatory changes, although greater in CBD. The activated GFAP+ astrocytes and microglia/macrophages in CBD were distributed extensively in S/M-FG and BG, with S/M-FG WM more affected. In PSP, abundant neuroinflammation was found in BG. The involvement of vasculature type was distinct among the two 4R-tauopathies, while CBD showed comparable proinflammatory changes in arterioles and venules, PSP exhibited predominant proinflammation in venules. The regional pattern of perivascular proinflammation differed between PSP and CBD, corresponding to the characteristic affected brain regions. CBD had more severe perivascular proinflammation that involved both arterioles and venules, while venules were more affected in PSP. Perivascular proinflammation may be a critical pathophysiological process in 4R-tauopathies.

items.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
items.authors: Qinfen Wu; Junhua Hu; Naibijiang Abuliezi; Yihan Sun; Yanyan Wu; Xiaoyi Dun
items.abstract: Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, and mesenchymal stem cell-treated samples. In this exploratory dataset, the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion samples showed relatively greater representation of inflammatory and antigen-presenting microglial states and elevated expression of selected microglial state-associated genes, including Slfn4, Apoe, and Gpnmb. In the corresponding exploratory comparison, the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample showed relatively greater representation of homeostatic-associated and Lgals3/Spp1-enriched microglial states and lower expression of several inflammatory-associated genes. Spatial mapping further revealed regionally restricted expression of microglial and neuronal markers within the injured tissue. Excitatory neurons displayed preliminary mesenchymal stem cell-associated transcriptional patterns involving mitochondrial transcripts, oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic signaling, calcium-related functions, and apoptosis/autophagy-associated pathways. CellChat analysis computationally predicted relatively high levels of tumor necrosis factor, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, and complement signaling in the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion sample, whereas the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample had relatively high levels of predicted activity of neuregulin, pleiotrophin and selected semaphorin. Together, these integrated datasets provide a hypothesis-generating framework linking microglial state remodeling, neuronal metabolic and synaptic programs, and predicted neuroimmune communication patterns after ischemic stroke. Because each omics condition or time point was represented by one biological sample, all the transcriptomic findings should be considered preliminary and exploratory and should be validated in independently replicated cohorts.

items.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
items.authors: Rademene Sunday Oria; Ugochukwu Godfrey Esomonu; Kenneth Igbang Sunday; Peter Arinze Oge
items.abstract: Heavy metal exposure has emerged as a significant environmental contributor to neurodegenerative disease, and a substantial body of mechanistic evidence implicates microglia in the pathological cascades that follow. Lead, cadmium, arsenic, manganese, copper, cobalt, mercury, and zinc disrupt central nervous system homeostasis through multiple cellular targets, but the resident innate immune cells of the brain are well placed to translate these insults into sustained neuroinflammation. Evidence for this critical narrative review was assembled through a purposive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Google Scholar for mechanistically informative studies reporting glial endpoints, with reference lists searched by hand and no systematic protocol applied. This review synthesizes current understanding of how individual metals engage microglial signaling networks, with particular attention to oxidative stress, NF-κB activation, NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, MAPK cascades, and suppression of the Nrf2 antioxidant axis. We examine the phenotypic spectrum that extends well beyond the classical M1/M2 dichotomy, including disease-associated microglia, lipid-droplet-accumulating microglia, and interferon-responsive states, and consider how metal-specific signatures map onto these transcriptional programs. Manganese-driven inflammasome assembly, cadmium-induced mitochondrial impairment, lead-mediated disruption of calcium homeostasis, and mercury-evoked autophagic dysfunction are discussed as illustrative examples of mechanistic divergence within a common neuroinflammatory framework. Glial responses to metal mixtures, which better represent real exposure than single-element designs, are considered separately, and the evidence for greater-than-additive effects is appraised. Downstream consequences for astrocyte reactivity, blood-brain barrier integrity, synaptic remodeling, and neuronal viability are placed in the context of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Therapeutic avenues are appraised, including chelation, natural antioxidants, NLRP3 inhibitors, TREM2 modulation, and microglial replacement strategies. Methodological constraints, particularly the overreliance on BV-2 cells and acute high-dose exposure paradigms, are critically considered. The review concludes by identifying priorities for translational research, including longitudinal human cohort studies, single-cell transcriptomic profiling of metal-exposed microglia, and the development of region-specific exposure models that better reflect chronic environmental realities.

items.title: Two-color, laser-induced fluorometry for evaluating the efficiency of click chemistry-based labeling of extracellular vesicles.
items.journal: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
items.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes, have attracted considerable attention as promising biomarkers for the early diagnosis and prognosis of cancer. In this study we evaluated the efficiency of a click chemistry-based EV labeling method using a two-color laser-induced fluorometry (LIF) system. During cell culture, cellular membranes were metabolically functionalized with azide groups, and the released EVs were subsequently labeled with Cy5 via click chemistry. The collected EVs were then stained with a phycoerythrin-conjugated anti-CD63 antibody (PE-anti-CD63) to achieve dual labeling. A two-color LIF system equipped with 488- and 635-nm lasers was used to distinguish Cy5-labeled, CD63-positive EVs from Cy5-unlabeled, CD63-positive EVs. Because PE and Cy5 are selectively excited at 488 and 635 nm, respectively, Cy5-labeled, CD63-positive EVs generated coincident dual-color fluorescence, whereas Cy5-unlabeled, CD63-positive EVs emitted fluorescence only upon 488-nm excitation. Using this platform, we investigated the effect that serum concentration in the culture medium exerts on click-chemistry labeling efficiency for CD63-positive EVs. The highest labeling efficiency for both HeLa and A549 cells was obtained in medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum. These findings demonstrate the utility of the proposed two-color LIF system for quantitatively evaluating the click-chemistry labeling efficiency of CD63-positive EVs under different cell-culture conditions.

items.abstract_cn: 细胞外囊泡（EV），包括外泌体，作为癌症早期诊断和预后的有前景的生物标志物而引起了广泛关注。在这项研究中，我们使用双色激光诱导荧光 (LIF) 系统评估了基于点击化学的 EV 标记方法的效率。在细胞培养过程中，细胞膜通过叠氮基团进行代谢功能化，释放的 EV 随后通过点击化学用 Cy5 进行标记。然后用藻红蛋白缀合的抗CD63抗体（PE-抗CD63）对收集的EV进行染色以实现双重标记。使用配备 488 nm 和 635 nm 激光器的双色 LIF 系统来区分 Cy5 标记的 CD63 阳性 EV 与 Cy5 未标记的 CD63 阳性 EV。由于 PE 和 Cy5 分别在 488 和 635 nm 处选择性激发，Cy5 标记的 CD63 阳性 EV 产生一致的双色荧光，而 Cy5 未标记的 CD63 阳性 EV 仅在 488 nm 激发下发射荧光。使用该平台，我们研究了培养基中血清浓度对 CD63 阳性 EV 的点击化学标记效率的影响。 HeLa 和 A549 细胞在添加 10% 胎牛血清的培养基中获得最高标记效率。这些发现证明了所提出的双色 LIF 系统在定量评估不同细胞培养条件下 CD63 阳性 EV 的点击化学标记效率方面的实用性。

items.title: Intraventricular clindamycin enhances interstitial brain fluid drainage and the blood-brain barrier after a traumatic brain injury.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
items.authors: Landon S Ashby; Megan G Crowe; Daveraj Chakravarty; Sanjeev Medam; Gabriel Frampton; Ayesha B Das; David A Hormuth; Thomas E Yankeelov
items.abstract: Despite advances in the acute clinical management of severe traumatic brain injuries (TBIs), treating injury-derived secondary pathogenesis remains challenging. We demonstrate intracerebroventricular (I.C.V.) administration of clindamycin alleviates TBI secondary pathogenesis in both focal and diffuse murine models of brain injury. I.C.V. administration of clindamycin increased the motility of ependymal cilia, which line the ventricles and spinal canal, by 30 to 60%, which correlated with interstitial brain fluid drainage through the cortex (r > 0.9 Pearson, n = 4 compounds tested). I.C.V. clindamycin treatment post-TBI also restored the blood-brain barrier (BBB), decreased lesion size, and lowered serum levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein by 2.8-fold. Consistent with these data, a novel objective recognition test revealed an improvement in recognition memory in brain-injured mice treated with clindamycin. These collective findings reveal a counterintuitive finding that I.C.V. clindamycin enhances drainage of toxins from the brain while simultaneously restoring the BBB, potentially providing a new solution for alleviating secondary pathogenesis in brain-injured patients.

items.title_cn: 脑室内注射克林霉素可增强脑外伤后间质脑液引流和血脑屏障。
items.abstract_cn: 尽管严重创伤性脑损伤（TBIs）的急性临床治疗取得了进展，但治疗损伤引起的继发性发病机制仍然具有挑战性。我们证明，在局灶性和弥漫性脑损伤小鼠模型中，脑室内 (I.C.V.) 给予克林霉素可减轻 TBI 继发性发病机制。 I.C.V.给予克林霉素可使脑室和椎管内的室管膜纤毛的运动性增加 30% 至 60%，这与通过皮质的间质脑液引流相关（r > 0.9 Pearson，n = 4 种测试化合物）。 I.C.V. TBI 后的克林霉素治疗还可以恢复血脑屏障 (BBB)、缩小病变大小并将神经胶质纤维酸性蛋白的血清水平降低 2.8 倍。与这些数据一致，一项新颖的客观识别测试显示，接受克林霉素治疗的脑损伤小鼠的识别记忆有所改善。这些集体发现揭示了一个违反直觉的发现：I.C.V.克林霉素可增强大脑中毒素的排出，同时恢复血脑屏障，这可能为减轻脑损伤患者的继发性发病机制提供新的解决方案。

items.title: Combined vitamins C and E attenuate memory impairment and hippocampal damage in diabetic sleep-deprived mice: behavioral and molecular insights.
items.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
items.authors: Fatemeh Habibnia; Olia Hamzeh; Manochehr Ashrafpour; Danial Habibi; Fereshteh Pourabdolhossein
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) and sleep disturbances are associated with cognitive impairment and hippocampal dysfunction, potentially involving oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the effects of vitamins C and E, individually and in combination, to determine whether their complementary antioxidant properties provide enhanced neuroprotective effects against cognitive and hippocampal alterations in diabetic sleep-deprived mice. METHODS: Diabetes was induced in male BALB/c mice (25-30 g) by streptozotocin (60 mg/kg), followed by partial sleep deprivation using the inverted flowerpot method. Animals received vitamin C (50 mg/kg), vitamin E (100 mg/kg), or their combination for 20 days. Body weight and blood glucose were monitored. Spatial learning and memory were evaluated using the Morris water maze. Hippocampal histopathology, GFAP immunostaining, and expression of genes related to oxidative stress, inflammation, and neuroprotection were assessed. RESULTS: Vitamin E and combined vitamin C and E treatment reduced FBG and were associated with higher final body weight than untreated diabetic sleep-deprived mice. Vitamin treatments improved spatial learning and memory, with combined treatment producing greater improvements in selected behavioral outcomes. Combined treatment increased hippocampal neuronal density and reduced GFAP immunoreactivity. Vitamin treatment increased BDNF, Nrf2, and HO-1 expression and reduced iNOS, TNF-α, and IL-1β expression. CONCLUSION: Vitamin C and E, particularly in combination, were associated with improved metabolic, cognitive, and hippocampal outcomes in diabetic sleep-deprived mice, potentially involving modulation of neuroinflammatory and oxidative stress-related markers.

items.title: Recombinant RANKL protects against brain injury in intracerebral haemorrhage by regulating microglial phenotypes via the STAT3 pathway.
items.authors: Ling Li; Juanjuan Li; Zhenning Tang; Xiaofang Bi; Jing Li; Yinbing Zhao; Kunmei Liu
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) is a severe stroke subtype with high morbidity and mortality, where inflammation plays a crucial role. Recent studies suggest that the RANKL/RANK pathway is involved in stroke pathophysiology. This study investigated the effects of recombinant RANKL on microglial polarization after ICH. METHODS: In vitro, BV2 cells were stimulated with erythrocyte lysis (ELS) to assess cell viability, migration, and microglial phenotype markers. Stattic was used to block STAT3 pathway, and microglial markers were measured by RT-qPCR. In vivo, ICH rats were treated with RANKL or OPG. Neurological deficits and brain injury were evaluated. Immunohistochemistry analysed microglial activation and M1/M2 marker expression. RESULTS: Recombinant RANKL enhanced BV2 cell migration induced by ELS and shifted microglial polarization towards M2, with reduced M1 marker expression. The increase in M2 markers was inhibited by Stattic, which blocks STAT3 signalling. In vivo, RANKL-treated rats showed reduced brain edema and improved neurobehavioral outcomes after ICH. RANKL treatment promoted M2 polarization of microglia/macrophages and inhibited M1 polarization following ICH. CONCLUSIONS: RANKL plays a key role in ICH by promoting microglia M2 polarization and inhibiting M1 polarization.

items.title_cn: 重组 RANKL 通过 STAT3 途径调节小胶质细胞表型，防止脑出血时的脑损伤。
items.abstract_cn: 背景：脑出血（ICH）是一种严重的中风亚型，具有高发病率和死亡率，其中炎症起着至关重要的作用。最近的研究表明 RANKL/RANK 通路参与中风病理生理学。本研究研究了重组 RANKL 对 ICH 后小胶质细胞极化的影响。方法：在体外，用红细胞裂解 (ELS) 刺激 BV2 细胞，以评估细胞活力、迁移和小胶质细胞表型标记。使用Stattic阻断STAT3通路，并通过RT-qPCR测量小胶质细胞标记物。在体内，ICH 大鼠接受 RANKL 或 OPG 治疗。评估神经功能缺损和脑损伤。免疫组织化学分析了小胶质细胞活化和 M1/M2 标记物表达。结果：重组 RANKL 增强了 ELS 诱导的 BV2 细胞迁移，并将小胶质细胞极化转向 M2，同时减少了 M1 标记物的表达。 M2 标记物的增加受到 Stattic 的抑制，Stattic 会阻断 STAT3 信号传导。在体内，RANKL 治疗的大鼠在 ICH 后表现出脑水肿减轻和神经行为结果改善。 RANKL 治疗促进小胶质细胞/巨噬细胞的 M2 极化，并抑制 ICH 后的 M1 极化。结论：RANKL 通过促进小胶质细胞 M2 极化和抑制 M1 极化在 ICH 中发挥关键作用。

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Yueman Zhang; Yonghui Chen; Yue Cheng; Ruqi Li; Weijie Chen; Yan Li; Qiuyue Fan; Yuxi Zhou
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Brain myeloid cells, including infiltrating monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) and microglia, play critical roles in ischemic brain injury, clearing debris and shaping neuroinflammation and neurological outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, using single-cell RNA sequencing and fate mapping with an MDM-specific Ms4a3creERT2-Ai14 mouse line, we identified serotonin receptor Htr2b+ MDMs as a crucial cell population involved in resolving neuroinflammation within the ischemic penumbra. Htr2b+ MDMs significantly accumulate in the peri-infarct region and exhibit enhanced phagocytosis and inflammation-resolving gene signatures. Mechanistically, Htr2b activation promotes nuclear translocation of Tfe3, a key lysosomal regulator, enhancing lysosomal biogenesis and supporting phagocytic activity. MDM-specific Htr2b ablation impairs debris clearance, exacerbates neuroinflammation and ischemic injury, whereas pharmacological agonism or Tfe3 activation restores lysosomal biogenesis in brain MDMs and improves post-stroke outcomes. Thus we demonstrate a previously unrecognized Htr2b+ MDM subset that integrates serotonin signaling to license intrinsic phagocytic function, alleviating ischemic brain injury.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Brain-sensing synNotch-CAR T cells enable precise targeting and clearance of diffuse midline glioma in multiple preclinical models.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Senthilnath Lakshmanachetty; Milos S Simic; Payal B Watchmaker; Robert Zhu; Takahide Nejo; Maggie Colton Cove; Jeffrey Haegelin; Haoyu Long
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a lethal pediatric brain tumor with limited therapeutic options and a poor prognosis. The success of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy requires both improving T cell tumor infiltration and persistence and reducing the risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Here, we adapted and advanced a brain-restricted CAR T cell platform previously validated in glioblastoma to address the anatomical and biological challenges of DMG. We engineered a T cell circuit in which a brain-specific synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptor recognizing brevican (BCAN) induced CAR expression against EphA2 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC"), thereby restricting CAR expression to the central nervous system (CNS). In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival. An alternative BCAN-primed CAR targeting B7-H3 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC-B/I") similarly improved therapeutic efficacy when delivered intravenously. However, icv administration triggered fatal neurotoxicity because of low-level B7-H3 expression in nontumor CNS regions, indicating that rapid CNS exposure via icv delivery can amplify off-tumor toxicity. In contrast, in an immunocompetent syngeneic DMG model, both iv and icv delivery of a murinized BCAN-gated B7-H3 CAR (mB-SYNC-B7-H3) achieved durable tumor clearance and resistance to rechallenge without any detectable neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, synNotch-primed CAR T cells exhibited reduced exhaustion, enhanced activation, and enrichment of naïve and stem cell memory-like subsets. These findings demonstrate that brain-sensing synNotch CAR T circuits represent a generalizable and translatable strategy for targeting multiple CNS malignancies, including DMG.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: TREM2: friend or foe in glioma?
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Mekenzie M Peshoff; Dolores Hambardzumyan; Long-Jun Wu
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is a neuroimmune signaling hub involved in key cellular processes including microglial phagocytosis, chemotaxis, and inflammation. Dysregulation of TREM2 has been implicated in a variety of diseases, most notably in the innate immune response to neurodegenerative disorders and cancer. The TREM2 pathway plays a significant role in governing microglia phenotypic transitions in Alzheimer's disease, as well as in regulating tumor-associated macrophages' ability to modulate cytotoxic activity. However, TREM2's role can be dependent on experimental parameters and disease contexts. Due to its intricate involvement in related disorders and the myeloid-dominated microenvironment in brain tumors, TREM2 has emerged as a vital player to better understand neuroimmune contributions to central nervous system malignancies. This review critically evaluates TREM2's controversial function in gliomas, analyzes experimental and biological variables that may underlie divergent findings, and outlines important considerations for future investigations.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: The TBK1-OTUB2-IRF3 signalling complex promotes neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Jianzhao Zhang; Deqi Wang; Jiaqing Chen; Yantong Lu; Deyu Deng; Beining Xu; Yanqi Xu; Keshuo Jin
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway-mediated chronic inflammation drives neurodegeneration in natural aging and various neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Here, we identify Otubain-2 (OTUB2) as a pivotal regulator that orchestrates the STING signalosome to amplify inflammatory responses. top_journal_neuroscience.title: Alzheimer's disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Emil Uffelmann; Douglas P Wightman; Shahram Bahrami; Alexey A Shadrin; Vera Fominykh; Takafumi Ojima; Chenyang Jiang; Christian Benner
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia, with global case numbers projected to reach 153 million in 20501. AD is highly heritable, with twin-based heritability estimates of 60-80%2. Although 1,200 causal loci are predicted to exist for AD3, approximately 80 loci have been associated with AD in two recent studies4,5. Low single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based heritability estimates have prompted the suggestion that little further common-variant risk remains to be found6. Here we analysed data from 109,479 cases, 74,141 proxy cases, 2,131,799 controls and 499,708 proxy controls from diverse ancestries, identifying 118 loci in a multi-ancestry analysis and 9 additional loci in ancestry-specific analyses, 48 of which are new. We identified new AD risk genes, prioritized potential drug targets, and found that genes upregulated in microglia and downregulated in neurons in cases compared with controls were enriched for AD-associated genetic risk. Moreover, we improved polygenic prediction and estimated a SNP heritability of 16%, nearly threefold higher than previous estimates. Together, our findings show that the common-variant contribution to AD has been substantially underestimated, and reveal new molecular and cellular mechanisms as well as specific targets for future drug development research.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Shimeng Zhang; Xiaoqing Gong; Songhai Tian; Yang Yang; Xinru Tong; Kuanwei Sheng; Yifan Zhang; Sho Amatsu
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in NEC pathogenesis3-5, the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin-CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Alzheimer's pathology mediates arteriolosclerosis and cerebral amyloid angiopathy associations with cognition.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Cellas A Hayes; Anhiti Dharmapuri; Chidera Agwu; Veronica Ramirez; John Newman; Meagan Chambers; Michelle C Odden; Kyan Younes
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Vascular and neurodegenerative pathologies frequently co-occur in aging brains, yet the mechanisms linking vascular neuropathologies to cognitive impairment remain incompletely understood. We examined whether Alzheimer's disease neuropathologic change (ADNC) and Lewy body disease (LBD) mediate or modify associations between vascular neuropathologies and domain-specific cognitive performance. The analytic sample included 1,269 decedents (mean age at death, 84.3 ± 9.1 years; 43.3% female; 94.7% White). At the last evaluation prior to death, 22.5% were cognitively normal, 2.4% were impaired but not mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 14.9% had MCI, and 60.2% had dementia. Vascular neuropathologies included arteriolosclerosis, atherosclerosis of the circle of Willis, cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), gross infarcts/lacunes, and microinfarcts. Multivariable linear regression models evaluated associations with harmonized memory, executive function, and language z-scores adjusting for age at death, sex, education, and apolipoprotein E ε4 status. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was tested. Mediation models estimated indirect and direct effects of vascular neuropathologies on cognition through ADNC or LBD using 5,000 bootstrap samples. Greater arteriolosclerosis severity was associated with worse memory (β=-0.16, 95% CI -0.23 to -0.09), executive function (β=-0.18, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.11), and language (β=-0.18, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.12; all p<0.001). CAA was strongly associated with poorer cognition across domains, including memory (β=-0.26, 95% CI -0.33 to -0.19; p<0.001). Atherosclerosis and infarcts showed more limited associations, while microinfarcts were not significantly associated with cognition. Mediation analyses indicated that ADNC statistically accounted for approximately 13-29% of the associations between arteriolosclerosis and cognition across domains and 64-91% of the associations between CAA and cognition. Direct effects of arteriolosclerosis remained significant, whereas CAA effects were largely explained by ADNC. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was limited, although LBD attenuated associations of arteriolosclerosis and CAA with executive function. Mediation through LBD was not observed. This novel evidence shows that vascular neuropathologies influence cognition through defined pathways with statistically significant patterns of associations. In this autopsy-confirmed cohort, vascular neuropathologies showed different patterns of association with domain-specific cognitive performance and ADNC. A larger proportion of the association involving CAA was statistically accounted for by ADNC, whereas direct associations remained more apparent for arteriolosclerosis. This study clarifies how vascular and neurodegenerative processes interact to shape cognitive impact and inform mechanistic preventions.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Dengue virus controlled human challenge reveals that preexisting immunity shapes viral replication and broadly protective responses.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Camila D Odio; Rosemary A Aogo; Saba Firdous; Charlie Voirin; Silvia Blanco-Rivera; Kelsey E Lowman; Nhyira Asante; Ysabelle Broderson
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Dengue is the canonical viral disease for which immune history is a determinant of protective versus pathogenic responses and immunogenicity. Yet, because of limitations in animal models and clinical presentation after peak viremia, how preinfection and early immune responses affect dengue outcome is not confirmed. We conducted a phase 1 clinical trial with 45 healthy adults to test whether secondary infection challenge with a heterotypic, full-length, attenuated virus increases viremia and immunogenicity compared with primary and tertiary infection. Viremia was associated with more, but still mild, clinical signs and symptoms, and secondary infection resulted in greater viremia, neutralizing antibodies, and protective T cell responses. However, those whose baseline antibodies most efficiently increased dengue virus replication in an in vitro assay experienced delayed inflammatory and adaptive immune activation, the highest viremia, strong acute immune responses, and waning of potent CD8+ T cells and antibodies. In contrast, higher baseline antibodies against the nonstructural protein 1 of multiple serotypes predicted early interferon and balanced immune activation, viremia control, and development of enduring, potent B and T cells, revealing how vaccines can induce broad, long-lasting protection. Last, individuals with potent and neutralizing antibodies and IFN-γ+ T cells at baseline experienced minimal viral replication. Together, these findings demonstrate that controlled human challenge with dengue virus can delineate coordinated versus dysregulated acute immune responses and their effects on immunogenicity, informing therapeutic and vaccine strategies for dengue and other viral diseases.

top_journal_neuroscience.title_cn: 登革热病毒控制的人类攻击表明，预先存在的免疫力决定了病毒复制和广泛的保护性反应。
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract_cn: 登革热是一种典型的病毒性疾病，其免疫史是保护性反应与致病性反应和免疫原性的决定因素。然而，由于动物模型和病毒血症高峰后临床表现的局限性，感染前和早期免疫反应如何影响登革热结果尚未得到证实。我们对 45 名健康成年人进行了一项 1 期临床试验，以测试与初次和三次感染相比，异型全长减毒病毒的二次感染攻击是否会增加病毒血症和免疫原性。病毒血症与更多但仍然轻微的临床体征和症状相关，继发感染导致更大的病毒血症、中和抗体和保护性 T 细胞反应。然而，那些基线抗体在体外试验中最有效地增加登革热病毒复制的人经历了延迟的炎症和适应性免疫激活、最高的病毒血症、强烈的急性免疫反应以及有效的 CD8+ T 细胞和抗体的减弱。相比之下，针对多种血清型非结构蛋白1的较高基线抗体可预测早期干扰素和平衡免疫激活、病毒血症控制以及持久、有效的B和T细胞的发育，揭示了疫苗如何能够诱导广泛、持久的保护。最后，基线时具有强效中和抗体和 IFN-γ+ T 细胞的个体经历了最小的病毒复制。总之，这些发现表明，用登革热病毒进行的受控人类攻击可以描述协调与失调的急性免疫反应及其对免疫原性的影响，为登革热和其他病毒性疾病的治疗和疫苗策略提供信息。

global_hot_topics.authors: Wei Zhang; Xueqian Zhang; Chenghao Zhang; Xinyang Shi; Yiheng Deng; Yan Gao; Kaipeng Bi; Zheng Wang
global_hot_topics.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) demonstrates complex associations with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and ageing, though their interconnected molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify and validate diagnostic biomarkers at the intersection of these pathways to enable early detection and risk stratification in high-risk populations. Bioinformatic analysis was performed on PCa and T2DM transcriptomic data downloaded from the GEO database, followed by differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. Eight machine learning algorithms were applied to identify hub ageing-related genes (ARGs), with SHAP analysis interpreting feature importance. A nomogram model was constructed and validated across multiple cohorts. Immune infiltration, drug sensitivity, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics were used for mechanistic exploration. Three key ARGs (SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4) were identified and used to develop a diagnostic model with high accuracy (AUCs: 0.726-0.905). SOX4 promoted immune evasion, PRNP exhibited context-dependent duality, and FOXO4 functioned as a tumor suppressor. Spatial and single-cell analyses revealed cell-type-specific expression and fibroblast-epithelial communication via MIF, LRP1, and FZD1. Drug sensitivity profiling identified abiraterone and docetaxel as potential therapeutics for high- and low-risk patients, respectively. In conclusion, SOX4, PRNP, and FOXO4 are key biomarkers linking PCa, T2DM, and ageing, and the diagnostic model shows robust performance and clinical utility, providing insights into microenvironment-driven mechanisms and personalized treatment strategies for PCa patients with T2DM.

global_hot_topics.title: Single-arm feasibility trial of manualized outpatient morita therapy for panic disorder with agoraphobia.
global_hot_topics.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
global_hot_topics.authors: Kiwako Yokoyama; Daisuke Yamaichi; Shigetsugu Nakao; Mitsuhiro Nakamura; Hiroyuki Uchida; Hidehito Niimura
global_hot_topics.abstract: AIM: This single-arm feasibility trial evaluated the feasibility and safety of a manualized outpatient Morita therapy (MT) program for patients with panic disorder (PD) and agoraphobia in routine psychiatric care, and explored preliminary signals of symptom change. METHODS: Ten outpatients with PD and agoraphobia were enrolled in a 12-session manualized MT program. Feasibility outcomes included retention, attendance, and therapist adherence. Exploratory outcomes were the changes in scores of the Panic and Agoraphobia Scale (PAS), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale-7 (GAD-7), the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and the Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36), assessed from baseline to the 6-month follow-up. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: Feasibility criteria were met. The completion rate was 90%, with a mean attendance of 11.6/12 sessions. Therapists reported high manual fidelity and usability. Exploratory analyses showed improvements in PAS (Hedges' g = 1.53, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.57-2.45) at 6-month follow-up, GAD-7 (g = 1.24, 95% CI 0.38-2.06), PHQ-9 (g = 1.05, 95% CI 0.25-1.80), and the Mental Component Summary of SF-36 (g = 1.71, 95% CI 0.68-2.70). The Role/Social Component Summary of SF-36 improved at post-treatment (g = 0.82, 95% CI 0.09-1.51) but not at follow-up (g = 0.45, 95% CI -0.19-1.06). No significant changes were observed in the Physical Component Summary of SF-36 (g = -0.14, 95% CI -0.72-0.46). CONCLUSION: Manualized outpatient MT appears feasible and safe for patients with PD and agoraphobia. Preliminary effects on symptoms warrant confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

global_hot_topics.title: Microglia-targeted delivery of MCC950 suppresses NLRP3-IL-18-mediated neuroinflammation and retinal injury in retinal vein occlusion.
global_hot_topics.authors: Xiao Xue; Huimin Jiang; Weiyue Zhang; Yifan Zhou; Hui Li; Chengbin Zhou; Yuxin Chen; Wei Ma
global_hot_topics.abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) causes retinal ischemia, macular edema, and vision loss, yet current anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies primarily limit vascular leakage and leave ischemia-driven neuroinflammation insufficiently controlled. Here, we reveal a critical role for microglia-associated NLRP3-IL-18 signaling in amplifying inflammation during early RVO. Bulk retinal RNA sequencing showed broad innate immune activation, whereas single-cell transcriptomic profiling and spatial protein analysis identified prominent inflammasome-related changes in retinal microglia. Constitutive global deletion of Nlrp3 or Il18 attenuated microglial activation and preserved retinal structure and electrophysiological function. To translate this mechanistic insight into a targeted anti-inflammatory strategy, we engineered MG1-functionalized, MCC950-loaded nanoliposomes for microglia-targeted NLRP3 inhibition. MG1 functionalization promoted preferential nanoparticle uptake by activated microglia and suppressed NLRP3-IL-18 signaling more effectively than free MCC950 or non-targeted nanoliposomes. In experimental RVO, a single intravitreal dose administered 6 h after induction alleviated retinal inflammation and edema while preserving retinal electrophysiological responses. These findings establish microglia-associated NLRP3-IL-18 signaling as a therapeutic target in early RVO and support MG1-MCC950 nanoliposomes as a bioactive nanotherapeutic platform for RVO.

global_hot_topics.title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomics reveals miR-941 targets CLDN4 to inhibit malignant progression of thyroid cancer through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
global_hot_topics.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
global_hot_topics.authors: Jinghua Zhou; Tiancheng Fu; Guoxiang Huang; Guangfeng Luo; Chengcheng Wang; Yanze Wang; Ziyang Ding; Xiarong Hu
global_hot_topics.abstract: Claudin-4 (CLDN4), a key tight junction protein, has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its functional role and regulatory mechanisms in thyroid cancer remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the contribution of CLDN4 to malignant progression and its interaction with the tumor-immune microenvironment. Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were integrated to identify CLDN4-associated malignant epithelial subpopulations. CLDN4 expression was validated in 25 paired papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) tissues by qRT-PCR, western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Functional assays were performed using CLDN4-overexpressing and CLDN4-knockdown B-CPAP and TPC-1 cells. The miR-941-CLDN4 interaction was verified by luciferase reporter assays. PI3K/AKT signaling and macrophage polarization were evaluated in vitro, and tumor growth was assessed in a xenograft mouse model. A CLDN4-high epithelial subpopulation was identified and associated with advanced tumor stage and PI3K/AKT activation. CLDN4 was upregulated in PTC tissues, whereas miR-941 was downregulated. High CLDN4 expression correlated with larger tumor size, lymphatic metastasis, and vascular migration. CLDN4 overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, colony formation, and apoptosis resistance, whereas knockdown produced the opposite effects. miR-941 directly targeted CLDN4 and attenuated its oncogenic effects. CLDN4 activated PI3K/AKT signaling, while PI3K inhibition reversed these phenotypes. CLDN4 also promoted M2 macrophage polarization and suppressed M1 polarization. In vivo, CLDN4 enhanced tumor growth, which was inhibited by PI3K blockade. miR-941 suppresses CLDN4 to inhibit PTC progression through modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway. These findings provide mechanistic insights into tumor progression and immune microenvironment remodeling, highlighting CLDN4 as a potential therapeutic target.

global_hot_topics.title: Targeting G2/M checkpoint vulnerability in homologous recombination-proficient tumors: lessons from ovarian cancer models.
global_hot_topics.authors: Qian Xi; Akiko Kunita; Saeko Nagai; Anh Quynh Duong; Masanori Kawakami; Katsutoshi Oda
global_hot_topics.abstract: Cell cycle dysregulation is a hallmark of cancer; however, tumors retaining homologous recombination (HR)-proficiency remain a major challenge. Although PARP inhibitors effectively target HR-deficient cancers, targeted therapies for BRCA1/2-wild-type, HR-proficient tumors are limited. High-grade serous ovarian cancer, approximately half of which is HR-proficient, illustrates that HR proficiency, together with replication stress and checkpoint dependence, may represent both a mechanism of therapeutic resistance and a druggable dependency on checkpoint-coupled DNA repair. This review synthesizes evidence that targeting either PLK1 or WEE1 independently exposes this vulnerability. PLK1 and WEE1 inhibition engage distinct mechanisms: PLK1 inhibition disrupts spindle assembly and HR competence, whereas WEE1 inhibition amplifies replication stress and forces premature mitotic entry. Nevertheless, both ultimately converge to compromise HR-associated repair, promote unresolved DNA damage, and trigger lethal mitotic catastrophe. Finally, we discuss biomarker-unselected trial failures, functional and replication stress-based patient stratification, and rational combinations with DNA-damaging agents and immunotherapy.

global_hot_topics.abstract_cn: 细胞周期失调是癌症的一个标志；然而，肿瘤保持同源重组（HR）能力仍然是一个重大挑战。尽管 PARP 抑制剂能有效靶向 HR 缺陷的癌症，但针对 BRCA1/2 野生型、HR 丰富的肿瘤的靶向治疗有限。高级别浆液性卵巢癌，其中大约一半是 HR 熟练的，这表明 HR 熟练程度以及复制应激和检查点依赖性可能代表了治疗耐药机制和对检查点偶联 DNA 修复的药物依赖性。本次审查综合了证据，表明针对 PLK1 或 WEE1 会独立暴露此漏洞。 PLK1 和 WEE1 抑制涉及不同的机制：PLK1 抑制会破坏纺锤体组装和 HR 能力，而 WEE1 抑制会放大复制压力并迫使过早进入有丝分裂。然而，两者最终共同损害 HR 相关修复，促进未解决的 DNA 损伤，并引发致命的有丝分裂灾难。最后，我们讨论了生物标志物未选择的试验失败、基于功能和复制压力的患者分层，以及 DNA 损伤剂和免疫疗法的合理组合。

global_hot_topics.title: Disease-specific gut microbiota-metabolite-immune networks in hematologic disorders: mechanisms, causal support, and translational strategies.
global_hot_topics.authors: Li Yi; Yuru Yuan; Xiaolong Ma; Chenxi Li; Yushuo Hao; Qianran Ma; Xuexue Liu; Xiao Du
global_hot_topics.abstract: The gut microbiota is increasingly recognized as a systemic regulator of host immunity, host metabolism, epithelial barrier integrity, and distal tissue homeostasis. Hematologic disorders provide an important setting in which these host-microbe interactions converge on immune remodeling, marrow-niche function, hematopoietic recovery, treatment response, and transplant-related complications. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, clinical, and translational evidence linking gut microbial dysbiosis to benign and malignant hematologic diseases, clonal and premalignant states, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT)-related outcomes. Rather than treating microbiome associations as a single evidence category, we distinguish five complementary evidence strata: Mendelian randomization, experimental models, prospective human cohorts, randomized human interventions, and cross-sectional studies. These study designs address different causal questions and are interpreted as complementary rather than as a single linear hierarchy. We also separate microbial composition from microbial function: taxon-level enrichment or depletion is treated primarily as context-dependent and hypothesis-generating, whereas conserved functional pathways-including short-chain fatty acids, bile-acid transformation, tryptophan metabolism, microbial translocation and barrier dysfunction, and innate immune activation-provide the principal cross-disease mechanistic framework. We integrate disease-specific microbial features, functional mediators, immune and marrow consequences, and clinical outcomes into an author-constructed evidence map, while explicitly addressing bidirectionality, reverse causality, and translational readiness. Emerging applications include microbiota-based biomarkers, treatment-response prediction, fecal microbiota transplantation, probiotics and postbiotics, antibiotic stewardship, and microbiota-dependent modulation of drug metabolism.

global_hot_topics.title: Basic science and surgical timing for polytrauma patients.
global_hot_topics.journal: OTA international : the open access journal of orthopaedic trauma
global_hot_topics.authors: Emily Pedrick; Roman Pfeifer; Emil Schemitsch; Michel Teuben; Heather Vallier; Justin Haller; Hans-Christoph Pape
global_hot_topics.abstract: Polytrauma patients are a challenging cohort to treat because their multiple, potentially life-threatening injuries act synergistically with surgeries to affect cellular pathways necessary for survival. Current treatment algorithms and blood tests often fail to predict which patients will tolerate early fracture fixation and which patients will continue to deteriorate because of their injuries. Traditional laboratory tests in polytrauma patients have not been able to capture the nuances of cellular energy depletion, and lipidomics are now emerging as potential biomarkers to better categorize disease severity. Definitive treatment of fractures in polytrauma patients within 36 hours is recommended, but there is little consensus on the parameters necessitating "damage control" strategies. The IMPACT group recommends fixation within 24 hours and a dynamic treatment strategy rather than strict guideline adherence. In particular, patients with moderate to severe traumatic brain injury require cautious, individualized decision-making given their neurologic risks. The purpose of this review is to describe emerging diagnostic tools and treatment algorithms that are shifting the management of polytrauma patients from rigid protocols towards dynamic, individualized assessments.

global_hot_topics.title: Pressure-guided pneumatic radial compression and radial artery occlusion after transradial coronary procedures: a retrospective historical cohort study.
global_hot_topics.authors: Yuchan Hu; Chao Lv; Ting Zhou; Junlan Zhu; Chunyan Lu; Qun'er Lou
global_hot_topics.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate a pressure-measured pneumatic radial compression protocol and its association with radial artery occlusion (RAO) after transradial coronary procedures. DESIGN: This single-center retrospective historical cohort included 514 consecutive patients treated between February and December 2025. The control group received conventional screw-type compression with clinically guided staged adjustment (n = 260), whereas the observation group received pneumatic compression with quantitative pressure measurement and individualized staged adjustment (n = 254). The primary outcome was RAO at 24 h; RAO at 7 days and other clinical outcomes were secondary outcomes. RESULTS: The observation group had lower observed RAO rates than the control group at 24 h [2.8% (7/254) vs. 7.7% (20/260), p = 0.012] and 7 days [2.0% (5/254) vs. 5.4% (14/260), p = 0.040]. After Firth penalized logistic regression, the protocol remained associated with lower odds of RAO at 24 h (adjusted OR = 0.358, 95% CI: 0.143-0.809; p = 0.013). The observation group also had lower pain scores at 6 and 24 h (both p < 0.001), higher digital SpO2 values at 2, 4, and 24 h (all p < 0.001), higher primary hemostatic success [97.2% vs. 93.5%, p = 0.042], and fewer patients with puncture-site oozing [2.8% vs. 6.9%, p = 0.028] or at least one local complication [11.4% vs. 28.1%, p < 0.001]. CONCLUSIONS: Pressure-guided pneumatic compression was associated with lower observed RAO rates and more favorable hemostatic and local outcomes than conventional screw-type compression. STUDY REGISTRATION: This study was a retrospective cohort study and did not involve a prospective intervention; therefore, clinical trial registration was not required.

medical_news.abstract: A surprising discovery reveals that widely used anti-inflammatory drugs may unintentionally help dangerous viruses spread through the body. medical_news.abstract: Mayo Clinic scientists have uncovered surprising new insights into “zombie cells,” aging cells that linger in the body and contribute to inflammation and disease. Seven studies reveal why these cells are harmful and identify new strategies for targeting them, including a natural compound found in tomatoes. In aging mice, experimental treatments reduced inflammation and improved physical and brain health. The findings could open the door to therapies that combat some of the biological processes behind aging.
